findings.title: Occurrence context ignores the schedule_type display copy
findings.body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() on that copy. The returned context then sets "config" to monitor_environment.monitor.config, the original dict, so the display conversion is discarded. Issue occurrences therefore publish the raw schedule_type integer (for example 0/1) instead of "crontab"/"interval". The returned dict is also the live in-memory config object, so any later mutation of the event context config mutates the cached monitor instance. Return the modified copy.

findings.title: Incident opens without N consecutive failures
findings.body: try_incident_threshold treats failure_issue_threshold as a lookback window, then opens an incident whenever none of those rows are CheckInStatus.OK. It never requires len(previous_checkins) >= failure_issue_threshold, and it does not require every row in the window to be a failure status (ERROR, MISSED, or TIMEOUT). A new monitor whose config asks for 3 consecutive failures still flips to ERROR and creates a MonitorIncident on the first failure, because the query returns one row and that row is not OK. A window such as [IN_PROGRESS, ERROR] with threshold 2 also opens an incident after a single real failure, since IN_PROGRESS is not OK. That creates issues and fires monitor_environment_failed before the configured consecutive-failure count is met. Require a full window of failure statuses before transitioning status and creating the incident.
